pictures.description: The pig in yellow tucks straw into the wall of a straw house.
pictures.text: Three little pigs set out to build houses. The first pig chose straw. It was so light that his little house went up in no time.

pictures.description: The pig in green ties sticks together for a house.
pictures.text: The second pig tied sticks together. Soon he had a house too. When the wind blew, the sticks rattled.

pictures.description: The pig in blue builds a sturdy red-brick house.
pictures.text: The third pig laid one brick on top of another. His house took longer to build, but its walls felt strong and still.

pictures.description: The wolf blows the straw house apart and the pig in yellow runs away.
pictures.text: Along came a wolf. He huffed and he puffed, and the straw scattered. The first pig ran straight to his brother’s stick house.

pictures.description: Sticks fly from the second house as the wolf blows and two pigs run away.
pictures.text: The wolf huffed and puffed again. The sticks tumbled down, and both pigs ran to their brother’s brick house.

pictures.description: The wolf blows at the brick house while all three pigs watch safely from its window.
pictures.text: The wolf huffed and puffed until he ran out of breath. The brick house stood firm. At last he gave up, and the three little pigs were safe together.

pictures.description: Goldilocks peeks through the open door of a cottage in the woods.
pictures.text: Three bears went for a walk while their porridge cooled. A girl named Goldilocks found their cottage. She knocked, heard no answer, and peeked inside.

pictures.description: Goldilocks eats from the smallest of three bowls of porridge.
pictures.text: On the table were three bowls. The biggest bowl of porridge was too hot. The middle one was too cold. The smallest was just right, so she ate it all.

pictures.description: The smallest wooden chair breaks beneath Goldilocks.
pictures.text: Next she tried three chairs. The first two felt too big. The smallest felt just right, until it broke with a crack!

pictures.description: Goldilocks is curled up asleep in the smallest bed, beside two larger beds.
pictures.text: Upstairs were three beds. One felt too hard and one too soft. The smallest felt just right, and Goldilocks fell fast asleep.

pictures.description: Goldilocks wakes up and sees the three bears around the bed.
pictures.text: The bears came home and found an empty bowl and a broken chair. In the bedroom Baby Bear cried, “Someone’s been sleeping in my bed, and she’s still there!” Goldilocks opened her eyes.

pictures.description: Goldilocks runs down the path as the three bears watch from the cottage.
pictures.text: Goldilocks jumped out of bed, ran down the stairs and hurried home through the woods. The three bears watched her go.

pictures.description: The hare and the tortoise face each other at the start of a path.
pictures.text: “I’m the fastest animal here,” boasted the hare. “Then race me,” said the tortoise. They agreed to race along the meadow path.

pictures.description: The hare bounds ahead while the tortoise walks behind.
pictures.text: Off they went! In a few leaps, the hare was far ahead. The tortoise kept walking, one slow step at a time.

pictures.description: The hare curls up asleep under a tree by the path.
pictures.text: The hare looked back and thought, “I have time for a nap.” He curled up in the shade and soon fell asleep.

pictures.description: The tortoise walks past the sleeping hare.
pictures.text: Step by step, the tortoise came to the tree. He passed the sleeping hare and kept going.

pictures.description: The hare wakes as the tortoise nears the red finish ribbon.
pictures.text: When the hare woke, he saw the tortoise near the finish. He sprang up and ran as fast as he could.

pictures.description: The tortoise crosses the finish ribbon just before the hare.
pictures.text: Too late! The tortoise reached the ribbon first. “You never stopped,” said the hare. The tortoise smiled.

pictures.description: A girl in a red hood carries a basket and waves goodbye to her mother.
pictures.text: Little Red Riding Hood was taking a basket of food to Grandma. “Stay on the path,” said her mother. Red waved goodbye and set off.

pictures.description: Little Red Riding Hood meets a grey wolf at a fork in the path.
pictures.text: In the woods she met a wolf. He asked where she was going. When she told him, the wolf slipped away down a shorter path.

pictures.description: The wolf knocks at Grandma’s cottage as Grandma peeks from the window.
pictures.text: The wolf reached Grandma’s cottage first. Grandma saw him through the window and hid in the pantry. The wolf crept inside and put on her nightcap.

pictures.description: Little Red Riding Hood sees long wolf ears poking out of Grandma’s nightcap.
pictures.text: When Red arrived, someone was tucked up in Grandma’s bed. “What big ears you have!” she said. Then she saw a long grey nose and called for help.

pictures.description: A woodcutter holds the door as the wolf runs out in Grandma’s nightcap.
pictures.text: A woodcutter heard Red and opened the door. The startled wolf jumped out of bed and ran back into the woods.

pictures.description: Grandma and Little Red Riding Hood share food from the basket.
pictures.text: Grandma came out of the pantry and hugged Red. Then they opened the basket and shared the bread she had brought.

pictures.description: A tiny grey mouse climbs over the paw of a sleeping lion.
pictures.text: A lion was asleep in the shade. A little mouse scurried over his paw and woke him up.

pictures.description: The little mouse looks up at the lion from his great paw.
pictures.text: The lion caught the mouse in his great paw. “Please let me go,” said the mouse. “Perhaps I can help you one day.”

pictures.description: The lion lifts his paw and the mouse scampers away.
pictures.text: The lion wondered how such a small creature could help him. Still, he lifted his paw and let the mouse run free.

pictures.description: The mouse finds the lion trapped in a rope net.
pictures.text: Later the mouse heard a roar. He followed the sound and found the lion tangled in a net.

pictures.description: The mouse gnaws through the thick rope that traps the lion.
pictures.text: The mouse nibbled through one rope, then another. Soon there was a hole big enough for the lion to step through.

pictures.description: The lion and mouse face each other beside the torn net.
pictures.text: The lion stepped free. “Thank you, little friend,” he said. The mouse smiled up at him.

pictures.description: Three goats look across a bridge towards a green meadow.
pictures.text: Three billy goats had eaten nearly all the grass on their side of the stream. Across a bridge, the meadow was thick and green.

pictures.description: The smallest goat crosses the bridge as the troll peeks out from underneath.
pictures.text: Trip-trap went the smallest goat. “Who’s on my bridge?” called a troll. “Only me,” said the goat. “My bigger brother is coming.” The troll let him pass.

pictures.description: The middle-sized goat crosses while the troll calls up to him.
pictures.text: Trip-trap went the middle goat. “Who’s on my bridge?” called the troll again. “Only me,” said the goat. “Our biggest brother is coming.” The troll let him pass too.

pictures.description: The biggest goat and the troll stand face to face on the bridge.
pictures.text: TRIP-TRAP went the biggest goat. This time the troll climbed onto the bridge. “Stop!” he shouted. The biggest goat lowered his horns and stood his ground.

pictures.description: The biggest goat looks down as the troll splashes into the stream.
pictures.text: The troll rushed at the goat. The goat held firm, and the troll tumbled into the stream with a great splash.

pictures.description: All three goats eat tall green grass together beyond the bridge.
pictures.text: The troll waded safely to the bank and went away. The biggest goat joined his brothers, and all three ate their fill of sweet green grass.
